question: 'Abhinaya Darpana' by Nandikesvara is one of the main sources of textual material for the study of the technique and grammar of body movement in the __________dance.
solution:
The correct answer is __**Bharatanatyam**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Abhinaya Darpana** is a highly regarded text authored by **Nandikesvara**, focusing on the art of expression in classical Indian dance.
 
• The text serves as one of the foundational sources for understanding the **technique and grammar of body movements** in classical Indian dance forms, particularly **Bharatanatyam**.
 
• It elaborates on different aspects of dance, such as **mudras (hand gestures), postures, and facial expressions**, which are integral to classical dance performances. *Hence, Bharatanatyam is directly linked to this text.*
 
• **Bharatanatyam** is one of the oldest and most prominent classical dance forms of India, deeply rooted in Tamil Nadu's culture and tradition. Its techniques align closely with the principles described in the **Abhinaya Darpana**.
 
• The dance is known for its rigorous footwork, precise hand gestures, and expressive facial movements, all of which are extensively discussed in **Nandikesvara's text**. *Hence, Bharatanatyam is the correct answer.*
 
• Other classical dance forms like **Manipuri, Odissi, and Kathak** have their own distinctive styles and techniques. While they may share certain elements with Bharatanatyam, they are not primarily associated with the **Abhinaya Darpana**.
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Bharatanatyam.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **About Abhinaya Darpana:**

 
 
• **Abhinaya Darpana** is a crucial text authored by **Nandikesvara**, focusing on the art of expression and the grammar of body movements.
 
• It provides detailed insights into **mudras (hand gestures), rasas (emotions), and bhavas (expressions)**, which are essential for classical dance performances.
 
 
 
• **Bharatanatyam:**
 
 
• **Origin:** Bharatanatyam originated in **Tamil Nadu** and is considered one of the oldest classical dance forms.
 
• **Features:** It is characterized by intricate footwork, elaborate hand gestures, and expressive facial movements.
 
• **Application:** Traditionally performed in temples as a form of devotion, it has evolved into a popular stage art.
 
 
 
• **Other Dance Forms:**
 
 
• **Manipuri:** Originated in **Manipur**, characterized by graceful movements and devotion-centric themes.
 
• **Odissi:** Originated in **Odisha**, known for its lyrical movements and strong connection to temple sculptures.
 
• **Kathak:** Originated in **North India**, characterized by storytelling through rhythmic footwork and spins.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Connection of Abhinaya Darpana with Bharatanatyam:**

 
 
• **Bharatanatyam** aligns closely with the principles described in the **Abhinaya Darpana**, especially in the use of mudras, rasas, and bhavas.
 
• The text provides a detailed foundation for understanding the expressive elements integral to Bharatanatyam.
 
 
 
• **Historical Relevance:**
 
 
• **Classical texts:** Texts like **Natya Shastra** by Bharata and **Abhinaya Darpana** by Nandikesvara have played a significant role in shaping Bharatanatyam.
 
• **Temple dance tradition:** Bharatanatyam was performed in South Indian temples as an offering to the deities.
